# VAIB Free Phishing Email Analyzer — Full Project Notes

## Overview
VAIB Free Phishing Email Analyzer is a static, client-side web application published by VAIB Technical Tools. Its purpose is to help a user perform an initial inspection of suspicious email source. It is intended for awareness, learning and basic security triage. It is not a forensic email validation service.

Website: https://vaibcc.github.io/free-Phishing-Email-Analyzer/
Repository: https://github.com/vaibcc/free-Phishing-Email-Analyzer
License: MIT

## How to use
1. Open the application in a modern browser.
2. Paste the complete raw email source, or select a local .eml file.
3. Run the analysis.
4. Review sender fields, authentication clues, heuristic findings and extracted links.
5. Export the structured JSON report or use the browser print function to save a PDF.

## Analysis performed
The application parses common headers including From, Reply-To, Return-Path, Subject, Received, Authentication-Results and Received-SPF. It extracts unique HTTP/HTTPS URLs from the provided source. Its rule-based checks include missing or mismatched sender fields, urgency and credential-related language, reported SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, URLs that use literal IPv4 hosts, common URL shorteners, unencrypted HTTP, unusual/punycode/deep hostnames, missing Received trace headers and references to potentially executable attachment extensions.

The score is a weighted heuristic capped at 100. It is an indicator for prioritizing manual review, not a probability that a message is malicious. The presence or absence of any one indicator is not conclusive.

## Authentication and trust boundaries
SPF, DKIM and DMARC values are parsed from the supplied message headers. The application does not independently establish that those headers were added by a trusted receiving mail server. It does not perform DNS lookups, SPF evaluation, DKIM cryptographic signature verification, DMARC alignment validation or ARC chain validation. A sender can supply forged header text. Treat parsed authentication values as untrusted reported claims unless corroborated using trusted mail-system logs or headers obtained directly from the receiving mail platform.

## Privacy and network behavior
Email source is read and analyzed in the user's browser. No email body or header data is intentionally submitted to a VAIB backend or third-party analysis API. The stylesheet currently imports Google Fonts, which causes a browser request for font resources; this request does not include the email content. Users requiring a fully offline page can remove that import from styles.css.

## Known limitations
- No attachment binary extraction or malware scanning.
- No URL fetching, redirect expansion, reputation lookup or sandboxing.
- No live DNS or domain registration checks.
- No independent authentication validation.
- Heuristic rules may miss sophisticated attacks and may flag legitimate messages.
- The tool should not be used as the sole basis for incident closure or a security decision.

## Repository layout
- index.html — application markup and page metadata.
- styles.css — responsive dark interface.
- app.js — parsing, heuristic rules, report rendering and export behavior.
- robots.txt — crawler policy and sitemap declaration.
- sitemap.xml — public canonical page sitemap.
- llms.txt — concise AI-readable overview.
- llms-full.txt — this expanded project description.
- README.md — installation, deployment, privacy and limitations.
- LICENSE — MIT license text.

Project name: VAIB Free Phishing Email Analyzer.
Publisher: VAIB Technical Tools.
Source contributions should use sanitized sample messages only. Never publish real email content, personal data, credentials, tokens or confidential headers in issues or commits.
